Tonicizzare = trattare un grado come ton: Tonicize = treat a degree as the tonic for an instant.
La dominante del V è D7, che porta a Sol: The dominant of the V is D7, which leads to G. The dominant of the ii is A7, which leads to D minor. They are written V7/V and V7/ii, “V of V” and “V of ii”. They are the most used.

Modulare significa passare da una tonali: To modulate means to pass from one key to another and stay there: the new reference chord becomes the tonic. It is not a secondary dominant, which lasts an instant. Here the piece really changes home.

Una dominante secondaria porta a un acco: A secondary dominant leads to a chord and then you return to the previous key. In modulation, after the arrival, you stay in the new key for several bars and confirm it with a full cadence, for example Am – D7 – G in G major.
Cadenza nella nuova tonalità = modulazio: Cadence in the new key = modulation.
Una cadenza conferma il nuovo centro!: A cadence confirms the new centre!
Le tonalità vicine a Do maggiore sono qu: The keys close to C major are those with almost the same notes. They are G major (one sharp of difference), F major (one flat) and the three relative minors: A, E and D minor. With these the modulation sounds natural.
Vicine a Do: Sol, Fa, La min, Mi min, Re: Close to C: G, F, A min, E min, D min.
Più note in comune, più facile è il pass: The more notes in common, the easier the move!
Il passaggio più comune è quello alla to: The most common move is to the key of the dominant. From C to G only one note changes: F becomes F♯. The G major scale: G A B C D E F♯ G.

L’accordo pivot è un accordo che si trov: The pivot chord is a chord found in both keys. In C major Em is the iii, in G major it is the vi. It is used as a hinge: first you hear it in the old key, then in the new one.
Dopo il pivot si prosegue con gli accord: After the pivot you continue with the chords of the new key. To go from C to G you can play: C – Em – Am – D7 – G. Em is the pivot, D7 is the V7 of the new key and G its I.
Un altro modo è inserire la dominante de: Another way is to insert the dominant of the new key without preparation, like D7 after C, and arrive at G. You use the strength of the V7 to impose the new tonic, with no pivot chord.
D7 → G imposes the new key.

Si può passare da Do maggiore a Do minor: You can go from C major to C minor: same tonic, different mode. Or you can make a break: the phrase ends and the piece restarts in another key, often a tone higher. It is the “key change” of many pop songs.

Un modo si ottiene suonando le note di u: A mode is obtained by playing the notes of a major scale but starting from another degree. The notes of C major, starting from D, give D E F G A B C: it is the Dorian mode. The centre has changed and so has the sound.
Mode = major scale from another degree.
I sette modi si chiamano: ionico (dal 1°: The seven modes are called: Ionian (from the 1st degree), Dorian (2nd), Phrygian (3rd), Lydian (4th), Mixolydian (5th), Aeolian (6th) and Locrian (7th). Ionian is the major scale, Aeolian the natural minor.

La scala pentatonica ha cinque note inve: The pentatonic scale has five notes instead of seven. It is the most used in pop, rock and blues because it contains no semitone intervals: every note sounds good over the chord.
La pentatonica minore ha 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7. Si: The minor pentatonic is 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7. It is obtained from the major pentatonic by starting from the sixth note: C major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic use the same notes. It is the basic scale of the rock solo.
La scala blues è la pentatonica minore c: The blues scale is the minor pentatonic with one extra note: the lowered fifth (♭5), called the blue note. It is used as a passing note between the fourth and the fifth and gives the typical “dirty” sound of the blues.
La blue note è quella di passaggio!: The blue note is the passing one!
La scala esatonale ha sei note a distanz: The whole-tone scale has six notes a tone apart. It has no semitones and therefore no tonal centre: it sounds suspended, dreamlike. From C: C D E F♯ G♯ B♭. It is much used on dominants with an altered fifth.
Le scale diminuite sono due, e hanno ott: There are two diminished scales, and they have eight notes. The first alternates tone and semitone: C D E♭ F G♭ A♭ A B. It is used on the diminished chord. It repeats identically every three semitones.
La seconda variante parte dal semitono:: The second variant starts from the semitone: C D♭ E♭ E F♯ G A B♭. It is the “dominant” diminished scale: it is used on the dominant seventh, especially with the ♭9, ♯9 and ♯11 notes.

Tra il La♭ (♭6) e il Fa♯ (♯4) c’è una se: Between the A♭ (♭6) and the F♯ (♯4) there is an augmented sixth. This interval resolves outwards: the A♭ falls to G and the F♯ rises to G, and so you arrive at the same note, the octave of G, on the dominant.
Sesta aumentata → ottava sulla dominante: Augmented sixth → octave on the dominant.
Sopra la sesta aumentata si aggiunge una: Above the augmented sixth a third note is added (C, the 1) and the result is the Italian sixth: A♭ C F♯. Adding D gives the French, adding E♭ the German. The German sounds like an A♭7 but resolves to the dominant.
Quella tedesca è la più usata!: The German is the most used!
Un diminuito di passaggio è un accordo °: A passing diminished is a °7 chord inserted between two diatonic chords to link them with a chromatic movement. In C – C♯°7 – Dm7, the bass rises by semitones: C, C♯, D.
Il °7 può sostituire un V7♭9 senza la fo: The °7 can replace a V7♭9 without the root: B°7 in place of G7♭9 leads to C. It has four notes a minor third apart, so each note can act as the root and it can resolve in four directions.
Il °7 è simmetrico: ogni nota può fare d: The °7 is symmetrical: every note can be the root.
Le mediante cromatiche sono accordi le c: Chromatic mediants are chords whose roots are a third apart but which do not belong to the key. C major and E major have only one note in common (E). The move is unexpected, but sounds natural right away.

Riconosco a orecchio una scala simmetric: I recognise a symmetrical scale by ear.

Cerca nelle canzoni che conosci un momen: Look in the songs you know for a moment that surprises you: it is probably a chromatic chord.

Controlla che l’estensione non “scontri”: Check that the extension doesn't “clash” with the chord: the 11 on a major chord is often avoided.

Controlla sempre che le note guida (3 e: Always check that the guide tones (3 and 7) are the same.
Sostituire un accordo senza controllare: Substituting a chord without checking the function: Am7 can act as a tonic, not as a dominant.

I play Dm7 – D♭7 – CΔ in three keys.

Dimenticare dove cade il ritorno alla to: Forgetting where the return to the tonic falls in the last bars.

Alterna un accordo per quarte con uno pe: Alternate a chord in fourths with one in thirds: hear how the character changes.
